explanation: The 1945 election taught the democratic opposition that the regime would grant the form of a contest when it wanted something from abroad, and would grant nothing that decided one. It kept control of the rolls, the censorship and the count. The campaign for Norton de Matos was built on that reading. It went for the presidency rather than the Assembly, because the regime could not take a single national candidacy apart constituency by constituency, and it went early and in the open. It ended the same way and for the same reasons, which is why the atlas puts the two side by side.
